conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee, one of the neurology team. You're here because of a severe headache that hasn’t gone away. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been almost ten days now. It’s on the right side, sharp and throbbing. I’ve had headaches before, but this one won’t let up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And do you have nausea, sensitivity to light or sound?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all of that. I’ve been too nauseous to eat much. And yesterday, I threw up three times.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s tough. You mentioned it gets worse when you lie down or strain. Does it get better when you sit up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, definitely. Sitting helps a little. I also felt like my face and head were swollen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You had a spinal tap at another hospital recently. The pressure was high—29. Did that help at all?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It did, actually. I felt better afterward, but it came back after a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We’ll monitor that. Your blood pressure is quite high tonight—191 over 107. That could be making things worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been checking it at home. It’s been like that for days. I’m already on meds for it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and we’ve asked endocrinology to look at your hypertension. Given your history, they think it might be due to hyperaldosteronism.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds familiar. I’ve had low potassium before. Is that related?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Hyperaldosteronism can cause high blood pressure and low potassium. They started you on spironolactone briefly, but we’ll need more tests.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But right now, the headache is what’s killing me. Nothing’s helping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’re increasing your acetazolamide—Diamox—from 250 mg twice a day to 500 mg. That’s for pseudotumor cerebri, to lower spinal fluid pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on that before. It helps sometimes. But my propranolol was lowered recently—could that be part of it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good point. You were on 20 mg twice a day, but it was reduced to 10 mg once a day because of concern for slow heart rate. You said your heart rate is normally low?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, always. I’m a runner. My doctor said it was okay, but they still cut the dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to increase it back to 20 mg twice a day. It helps prevent migraines, and your heart rate is stable now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I really hope that helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the headache today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still bad. The meds aren’t touching it. I barely slept.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve reviewed your case. Since the headache sounds more like a severe migraine now, we’re going to try an IV medication—valproate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that safe? I’ve never had that before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s commonly used for severe migraines. We’ll give a single dose and monitor you closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling now, about 20 minutes after the infusion?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Actually… it’s a bit better. Not gone, but the pressure feels less.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s encouraging. We’ll keep monitoring. The endocrine team also restarted enalapril for your blood pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was on that before. Is it safe with my kidneys?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your kidney function is stable. We’ll watch it, but it should help control your pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs look stable. Headache any better?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still there, but not as intense. I’m able to drink water and eat a little.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s progress. We’re not seeing signs of worsening pseudotumor cerebri—no papilledema, your vision is intact.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So is it migraines then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely a transformed migraine—chronic and severe. The Diamox and propranolol should help prevent future ones.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you today. You’re doing much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. What about the headache?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s improved. We’re giving you a short course of oxycodone—five doses—just in case. But try to rely on your preventive meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your headache specialist soon. And endocrinology wants you to stop enalapril two weeks before your appointment for testing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you for helping me through this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call if the headache worsens or you have vision changes.
